provenance.notes: Researched definition in tools/extract/patterns/src/apg-2.mjs. Every binding was checked against the APG page; roles and key names are cross-checked mechanically against apg-skeleton.json and aria-roles.json. Arabic name is an unreviewed translation.

roles.on: item that runs a command or opens a submenu
item with an independent checked state
item in a mutually exclusive group

roles.note: Not focusable. Used to delimit a group of menuitemradio items.

attributes.name: aria-disabled
attributes.note: Disabled items stay focusable but cannot be activated.

attributes.name: aria-labelledby
attributes.values: IDREF of the menuitem or button that opens it; otherwise aria-label

attributes.name: aria-activedescendant
attributes.note: Alternative to roving tabindex; the container then has tabindex 0 or -1.

keyboard.action: On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its first item. Otherwise activate the item and close the menu.

On a menuitemcheckbox: toggle it without closing. On an unchecked menuitemradio: check it and uncheck the others of its group without closing. On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its first item. On any other item: activate it and close the menu.
Move focus to the next item, optionally wrapping from last to first.
Move focus to the previous item, optionally wrapping from first to last.
On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its first item. On an item without one: nothing, when the menu was opened from a menu button rather than a menubar.
In a submenu of a menu item: close the submenu and return focus to its parent item.
Move focus to the first item of the current menu.
Move focus to the last item of the current menu.
Move focus to the next item of the current menu whose label starts with the character.
Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to what opened it (menu button, parent item, or invoking context).
Move focus out of the menu to the next element in the page sequence and close all menus and submenus. Tab never moves focus into a menu.
Move focus out of the menu to the previous element in the page sequence and close all menus and submenus.

focus.entry: A menu is never reached by Tab: when it opens, the author moves focus to its first item (or the last, when opened with ArrowUp).
focus.exit: Escape closes the current level; Tab or Shift+Tab closes everything and leaves; activating an item closes all levels.
focus.restore: To the element that opened the menu; for a submenu, to its parent item.
focus.tabStops: None while closed; items have tabindex -1.
focus.note: aria-activedescendant on the menu container is the alternative. Disabled items are focusable; separators are not.

variants: menu opened by a menu button

keysNotBound.reason: Named as the Windows command that opens a context menu; see context-menu.
An example of an application shortcut that focuses a menubar from an editor; not a binding of the pattern.

rtlDecisions.question: Which arrow opens a submenu from a vertical menu, and which closes it, in RTL?
rtlDecisions.apg: Silent. No pattern page mentions right-to-left; keys are described physically (left, right) for a left-to-right layout. Right Arrow opens a submenu, Left Arrow closes it.

libraries.behaviour: In RTL ArrowLeft opens the submenu and ArrowRight closes it.
SUB_OPEN_KEYS and SUB_CLOSE_KEYS are keyed by direction: rtl opens with ArrowLeft, closes with ArrowRight.
List navigation takes an rtl flag; the cross-orientation open and close keys are ArrowLeft and ArrowRight respectively when rtl.
In a vertical menu Left means "children" (open) and Right means "parent" (close) when rtl.

rtlDecisions.reason: A submenu opens toward inline-end, which is the left in RTL; the arrow must point where the submenu appears.

data.notes: This file is the popup part of the APG "Menu and Menubar" page; menubar covers the bar. RTL: a submenu opens toward inline-end, so ArrowLeft opens and ArrowRight closes. In a horizontal menu (aria-orientation=horizontal) the vertical and horizontal arrows exchange roles, and the next/previous pair then mirrors instead.
